name: Crest Audio
notes: Dave Fox revived the Fuzz Face at Crest Audio, producing about 2,000 units from 1986-1990. Treat Crest as a distinct manufacturing/revival node, while preserving its Dallas Music Industries/Dallas Arbiter corporate lineage separately.

name: Skinpimp Hand Crafted
notes: Premier Guitar documented Ryan Kirkland's Skinpimp Hand Crafted as a boutique builder making close recreations of Tone Bender, Buzzaround and Fuzz Face models. The 2009 article provides a strong existence anchor but not a complete catalog or full production chronology.

name: North Effects
notes: Effects Database documents a North Effects Fuzz Face by builder Northwind. Exact legal identity, geography and broader catalog remain to be reconciled.

name: Gearmanndude
notes: Builder's own archived blog documents the Time Bomb Boost as a DOD 250 clone and records additional small-batch production, including a stated 50-pedal batch in 2010. Preserve as a builder and research the complete dirt catalog separately.

name: Greer Amps
notes: Greer describes the 390 as a DOD 250-derived overdrive created in response to an endorser request. Effects Database and Greer-era demo material document a first run of 30 and hand-wired production in Athens, Georgia. Exact complete catalog still requires Queue B.

name: Neo-Classic Effects
notes: FXDB's interview with Steve Mavronis documents Neo-Classic Effects in Baltimore and the 741 Overdrive as his first pedal project, begun after researching the vintage DOD 250. The builder later decided a home-based sales operation was impractical, making this a useful micro-builder preservation case.

name: ThunderTomate
notes: Effects Database indexes a ThunderTomate OD / Preamp 250 as a DOD 250-based product. Builder identity, geography and production history remain unresolved, so keep as discovery-only until independently corroborated.

name: Profi-Sound
notes: Effects Database links Yu Brother's OV-200 to Profi-Sound and separately indexes a Profi-Sound Overdrive Preamp and Tronix OV-200, explicitly flagging possible copy/OEM relationships. Preserve the entities as separate labels until manufacturing lineage is proven.

name: Tronix
notes: Rare OV-200 listing appears in the DOD 250 family tree with an explicit copy-or-OEM question. No manufacturing attribution is assumed; retain as a badge/OEM candidate for later lineage research.
